text:
acme-infra: Hey team, our customers are seeing NXDOMAIN for the private service endpoint (svc.acme.internal) from within their VPC since this morning. Public API works. Can you help triage?

maya_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the output of a few quick checks: `dig +short svc.acme.internal @169.254.169.253` (from a failing node), `kubectl get svc` if applicable, and `curl -v --resolve svc.acme.internal:443:<private-ip> https://svc.acme.internal/health`?

acme-infra: Sending outputs.
```
acme-infra: $ dig +short svc.acme.internal @169.254.169.253
acme-infra: ;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
acme-infra: ;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1
acme-infra: ;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
acme-infra: svc.acme.internal. 300 IN SOA ns-1.acme.internal. hostmaster.acme.internal. 1 7200 900 1209600 3600
```

acme-infra: And curl:
```
acme-infra: $ curl -v https://svc.acme.internal/health
acme-infra: *   Trying 10.80.5.12:443...
acme-infra: * Connected to 10.80.5.12 (10.80.5.12) port 443 (#0)
acme-infra: * TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
acme-infra: * TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
acme-infra: * error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
acme-infra: * Closing connection 0
acme-infra: curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```

maya_support: Thanks. NXDOMAIN from the VPC resolver suggests Route53 private hosted zone / resolver rules issue, but the TLS error after connecting suggests the endpoint IP answered but presented a cert the client doesn't trust — can you confirm whether you hit an ALB/NLB with a customer cert or an internal cert (managed by your infra)?

acme-infra: It's a private NLB in front of pods. The cert is ACM-private issued in our account. The cert used to work.

ethan_infra: Quick checklist: 1) Are there multiple private hosted zones with the same name across accounts? 2) Is the hosted zone associated with the customer VPC? 3) Any Route53 Resolver rules overriding resolution? 4) Node-local or dnsmasq cache returning stale NXDOMAIN?

priya_oncall: Also check egress allowlist on the VPC/SG/NAT: if UDP 53 or TCP 53 is blocked to the forwarder or to Route53 endpoints, some lookups will fail or fall back incorrectly.

acme-infra: We checked hosted zones: there is a private hosted zone svc.acme.internal in our account (hz-AAAA), associated with VPC-a (correct). But there's also a different private hosted zone with the same name in an older tenant account (hz-BBBB) — I didn't realize that was still present.

maya_support: Aha — that can cause split-horizon/shadowing. If the wrong hosted zone is associated with the VPC (or resolver rule points to another account), lookups can return NXDOMAIN or unexpected SOA. Can you `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name svc.acme.internal` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id hz-BBBB` to confirm associations?

acme-infra: Run outputs:
```
acme-infra: $ aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id hz-AAAA
acme-infra: { "HostedZone": { "Id": "hz-AAAA", "Name": "svc.acme.internal.", "Config": { "PrivateZone": true }, "VPCs": [{"VPCId":"vpc-0a1b2c","VPCRegion":"us-west-2"}] } }
acme-infra: $ aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id hz-BBBB
acme-infra: { "HostedZone": { "Id": "hz-BBBB", "Name": "svc.acme.internal.", "Config": { "PrivateZone": true }, "VPCs": [] } }
```

ethan_infra: hz-BBBB has no VPC associations — likely created by mistake and intended for a different env. However, if there are resolver rules or cross-account associations, hz-BBBB could still be shadowing via a Route53 Resolver outbound/inbound setup.

priya_oncall: Also dbl-check Route53 Resolver rules: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters ...` and `list-resolver-rule-associations`. If there's a rule that forwards queries for svc.acme.internal to a wrong IP (or to a DNS firewall), that'll cause NXDOMAIN.

acme-infra: Running resolver checks now.
```
acme-infra: $ aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=CreatorRequestId,Values=*
acme-infra: [ {"Id":"r-1111","DomainName":"svc.acme.internal","RuleType":"FORWARD","Status":"AUTOMATED","CreatorRequestId":"r1"} ]
acme-infra: $ aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=name,Values=*
acme-infra: [ {"Id":"rassoc-1","ResolverRuleId":"r-1111","VPCId":"vpc-0a1b2c","Name":"forward-to-onprem"} ]
```

maya_support: That rule forwards svc.acme.internal to an on-prem forwarder. If the on-prem forwarder returns NXDOMAIN (or is unreachable due to egress controls), the VPC resolver will report NXDOMAIN. Is the forwarder reachable?

acme-infra: The forwarder IPs are 203.0.113.10 and .11 — those are reachable from the VPC? Wait, we have a strict egress allowlist that only allows outbound to the customer's NAT pool on 443 and 80. No UDP/TCP 53 outbound allowed to those forwarders. Could be blocked.

ethan_infra: That matches. If the resolver rule points off-VPC to an on-prem DNS but egress is blocked, you'll get timeouts or NXDOMAIN depending on caching behavior. Two paths here: 1) allow egress to the forwarder IPs on TCP/UDP 53 (or TLS-DNS 853 if using DoT) OR 2) remove/adjust the resolver rule and associate the correct private hosted zone with the VPC so the record is authoritative in AWS.

priya_oncall: Given the TLS cert error earlier, once DNS is fixed you'll want to verify the cert chain is valid from inside the VPC — ACM Private certificates require trust in the private CA. If your nodes don't trust the issuing CA, TLS will fail even when DNS is correct. Check the server cert chain: `openssl s_client -connect 10.80.5.12:443 -servername svc.acme.internal -showcerts` and confirm the cert subjectAltName includes svc.acme.internal and the client trusts the CA.

acme-infra: Ran openssl s_client — the chain shows the ACM Private cert but the client doesn't have the private CA cert installed. We thought the AWS-managed CA would be auto-trusted inside the VPC, but our custom images don't include the company's internal root cert.

maya_support: Ok two separate issues: 1) resolver rule + egress allowlist causing NXDOMAIN, 2) missing internal CA trust causing TLS unknown CA. Steps to remediate:
- For immediate mitigation, disassociate the problematic resolver rule from the VPC (so Route53 private zone hz-AAAA takes precedence) OR update egress allowlist to allow DNS to the forwarder IPs.
- Install the internal CA certificate in your node image / container trust store so the ACM-private cert validates.
- Remove or delete the stray private hosted zone hz-BBBB if it's unused to avoid future confusion.

acme-infra: We'll try disassociating the resolver rule first.

dns-bot: [automation] Resolver rule association rassoc-1 disassociated from vpc-0a1b2c by maya_support at 1765554560

acme-infra: After disassociation, `dig` now returns the correct IP: `10.80.5.12` and `curl -v` shows TLS handshake succeeds (cert now trusted after we pushed CA cert to nodes). Service is reachable again. Thanks!

maya_support: Great — can you keep hz-BBBB flagged for deletion and add a note to runbook: check resolver rule associations and egress allowlists when private endpoint NXDOMAIN appears.

ethan_infra: I'll open a low-priority infra ticket to scan for duplicate private zones across org accounts and flag cross-account resolver rules that forward externally.

acme-infra: Thanks all. We'll follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

priya_oncall: closing loop — recommend adding `dig +trace` and `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations` to your incident playbook for faster triage. :white_check_mark:
